title: FATHER Future Lab — Method Passport Catalog

passports.name: Naive forecast
passports.algorithm: ŷ(t+h)=y(t) for a non-seasonal naive forecast
assumptions: historical pattern contains usable information about the near future
passports.conclusion: Use as transparent baseline or when data are limited; always compare with a naive benchmark and rolling backtest.
passports.qualification_rule: Requires source, algorithm, implementation/tests and relevant backtest.

passports.name: Historical mean
passports.algorithm: ŷ = arithmetic mean of historical levels
assumptions: stable level without material trend
limitations: poor under trend, seasonality or structural break
passports.conclusion: Use as transparent baseline or when data are limited; always compare with a naive benchmark and rolling backtest.
passports.qualification_rule: Requires source, algorithm, implementation/tests and relevant backtest.

passports.name: Drift method
passports.algorithm: extend the average change from first to last observation linearly
assumptions: approximately linear long-run change
passports.conclusion: Use as transparent baseline or when data are limited; always compare with a naive benchmark and rolling backtest.
passports.qualification_rule: Requires source, algorithm, implementation/tests and relevant backtest.

passports.name: Simple exponential smoothing
passports.algorithm: recursive exponentially weighted level with smoothing parameter α
assumptions: level process; no material trend or seasonality
passports.conclusion: Use as transparent baseline or when data are limited; always compare with a naive benchmark and rolling backtest.
passports.qualification_rule: Requires source, algorithm, implementation/tests and relevant backtest.

passports.name: Kalman-family state estimation
passports.algorithm: Formal algorithm to be finalized during qualification.

passports.conclusion: Strong for sequential state estimation; choose the filter variant to match system dynamics.
passports.qualification_rule: Requires source, algorithm, implementation/tests and relevant backtest.

passports.name: Bayesian probabilistic model

passports.name: Ensemble forecast and uncertainty

passports.name: Natal astrology

predicts: claims defined by the historical/divinatory rule system

passports.algorithm: historical astrology rule set only; scientific validation is not assumed
assumptions: rules are documented reproducibly
limitations: not scientifically validated as predictive evidence
must not influence scientific confidence or high-stakes decisions
passports.conclusion: Keep strictly separated as NON_SCIENTIFIC; may be tested experimentally but never labeled scientific.
passports.qualification_rule: May be reproduced as a cultural/historical algorithm for comparison, never labeled scientifically validated.

passports.name: Shortest path
passports.algorithm: shortest-path algorithms such as Dijkstra/Bellman–Ford depending on weight conditions
assumptions: graph accurately represents the system and weights
limitations: dynamic/stochastic networks may invalidate static solution
passports.conclusion: Use for structural optimization; it predicts consequences of network constraints rather than future time series by itself.
passports.qualification_rule: Discovery complete. Requires authoritative source, code, tests and qualification before RUNNABLE.

passports.name: Critical Path Method

passports.name: Mean absolute increment extrapolation
passports.algorithm: last value + horizon × mean absolute increment
assumptions: chain absolute increments are approximately constant
passports.conclusion: Use as transparent baseline or when data are limited; always compare with a naive benchmark and rolling backtest.
passports.qualification_rule: Educational source captured; qualify against authoritative time-series reference before RUNNABLE.

passports.name: Mean growth-rate extrapolation
passports.algorithm: last value × mean growth coefficient^horizon
assumptions: relative growth rate is approximately constant
passports.conclusion: Use as transparent baseline or when data are limited; always compare with a naive benchmark and rolling backtest.
passports.qualification_rule: Requires implementation, tests and authoritative-source qualification.

passports.name: Trend-line extrapolation
passports.algorithm: fit trend curve and evaluate it at future t
assumptions: historical pattern contains usable information about the near future
passports.conclusion: Use as transparent baseline or when data are limited; always compare with a naive benchmark and rolling backtest.
passports.qualification_rule: Requires explicit trend model selection, diagnostics, code and backtest.

passports.name: Forecast interval
passports.algorithm: model-specific point forecast ± uncertainty term
assumptions: interval formula matches the forecast model and error process
limitations: interval formula must match model; generic interval is unsafe
passports.conclusion: A point forecast without uncertainty is incomplete for consequential decisions.
passports.qualification_rule: Interval formulation must be tied to the selected forecasting model and qualified statistically.

passports.name: Simple average forecast combination
passports.algorithm: equal weights wi=1/K
assumptions: historical errors are informative about future performance
passports.conclusion: A surprisingly strong baseline for combinations; must be included in every ensemble benchmark.
passports.qualification_rule: Requires primary-source verification, implementation, tests and rolling-origin backtest before RUNNABLE.

passports.name: Trimmed mean forecast combination
passports.algorithm: remove selected extreme component forecasts, then average remaining forecasts
assumptions: historical errors are informative about future performance
passports.conclusion: Weights are a model of their own and must be trained/backtested separately from component forecasters.
passports.qualification_rule: Requires primary-source verification, implementation, tests and rolling-origin backtest before RUNNABLE.

passports.name: Simple linear regression
passports.algorithm: OLS fit of Y=β0+β1X+ε
assumptions: linear relation
errors centered around zero; classical inference adds homoscedastic/normality assumptions
limitations: extrapolation outside training range is risky
passports.conclusion: Useful when future predictors are available and relationships are stable; validate out of sample.
passports.qualification_rule: Requires source validation, implementation/test protocol and qualification appropriate to the method class.

passports.name: Multiple linear regression
passports.algorithm: OLS fit of Y=β0+ΣβiXi+ε
assumptions: functional form is adequate
training sample is representative
passports.conclusion: Useful when future predictors are available and relationships are stable; validate out of sample.
passports.qualification_rule: Requires source validation, implementation/test protocol and qualification appropriate to the method class.

passports.name: Ridge / Tikhonov regularized regression
passports.algorithm: minimize squared error + γΣβ² (Tikhonov/Ridge penalty)
assumptions: functional form is adequate

passports.name: Maximum likelihood estimation
passports.algorithm: choose parameters maximizing the likelihood of observed sample
assumptions: chosen likelihood family is appropriate
limitations: not itself a complete forecasting system
passports.conclusion: Treat as an estimation engine inside a forecasting model, not as an independent forecast.
passports.qualification_rule: Requires source validation, implementation/test protocol and qualification appropriate to the method class.

passports.name: Delphi expert forecasting

predicts: plausible future states / expert probability / strategic scenarios

passports.algorithm: iterative anonymous expert rounds with controlled feedback and revision
assumptions: sources and expert process are transparent
limitations: scenario planning is not a point forecast
expert bias and political incentives can distort results
passports.conclusion: Separate probability forecasts from scenarios and foresight; never present exploratory scenarios as predicted outcomes.
passports.qualification_rule: Requires source validation, implementation/test protocol and qualification appropriate to the method class.
